document.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
document.abstract: CLIP learns transferable image representations from image-caption pairs. Pairing prediction provides natural-language supervision without fixing a predefined set of classes. After training, descriptions of classes support zero-shot transfer across a broad range of visual recognition tasks.

document.title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation
document.abstract: BLIP addresses both discriminative understanding and text generation in vision-language pretraining. Its caption bootstrapping procedure creates synthetic descriptions and filters noisy captions from web image-text data. The framework transfers to retrieval, captioning, question answering, and video-language tasks.

document.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
document.abstract: Flamingo connects pretrained visual and language components to process images or videos interleaved with text. Training on multimodal web sequences enables adaptation from a small number of prompted examples. Evaluation covers image and video understanding, including visual questions and captions.

document.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
document.abstract: BLIP-2 reduces vision-language training costs by retaining pretrained image encoders and language models as frozen components. A lightweight querying Transformer bridges them through successive representation-learning and generative-training stages. The resulting model supports visual tasks and instruction-following image-to-text generation.

document.title: Multimodal Few-Shot Learning with Frozen Language Models
document.abstract: Frozen transfers a pretrained language model’s few-example prompting ability to visual tasks. A trained image encoder supplies continuous visual prefixes while the language model weights stay unchanged. Interleaved visual and textual examples enable few-shot question answering, new visual concepts, and object-word learning.

document.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
document.abstract: LLaVA studies instruction tuning for visual-language assistants. Language-only GPT-4 is used to create image-related instruction data, and a visual encoder is connected to a language model and trained with these examples. Experiments examine multimodal dialogue and science question answering.

document.title: MiniGPT-4: Enhancing Vision-Language Understanding with Advanced Large Language Models
document.abstract: MiniGPT-4 connects a frozen visual encoder to a frozen Vicuna language model through a trainable projection. Initial image-caption training is followed by tuning on curated detailed descriptions to improve generation quality. Demonstrations include image description, image-based conversations, and interpreting handwritten drafts.

document.title: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning
document.abstract: InstructBLIP investigates vision-language instruction tuning starting from BLIP-2. Public datasets are converted to instructions, with separate training and held-out task groups. Instruction-aware feature extraction adapts visual representations to the requested task. Evaluation emphasizes generalization to unseen tasks.

document.title: Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation
document.abstract: ALBEF aligns image and text representations through contrastive learning before cross-modal fusion. Momentum distillation supplies soft targets to improve learning from noisy image-text pairs. The approach avoids object-region annotations and is evaluated on retrieval and visual-language reasoning tasks.

document.title: ViLT: Vision-and-Language Transformer Without Convolution or Region Supervision
document.abstract: ViLT simplifies visual-language pretraining by removing convolutional feature extraction and supervised object regions. Images and text enter a shared Transformer with minimal visual preprocessing. The work investigates how this design affects efficiency and downstream multimodal performance.

document.title: Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision
document.abstract: ALIGN learns visual and textual representations from a large collection of noisy image alt-text pairs. A dual encoder uses contrastive supervision rather than costly curation of every pair. The representations support zero-shot classification and image-text retrieval.

document.title: SimVLM: Simple Visual Language Model Pretraining with Weak Supervision
document.abstract: SimVLM simplifies vision-language pretraining using weakly supervised data and a single prefix language-modeling objective. It avoids region labels and combinations of dataset-specific losses. The resulting pretrained model transfers to both discriminative and generative visual-language tasks.

document.title: VLMo: Unified Vision-Language Pre-Training with Mixture-of-Modality-Experts
document.abstract: VLMo uses modality-specific experts and shared self-attention within a modular Transformer. The same pretrained model can serve as a dual encoder for retrieval or a fusion encoder for classification. Stagewise training combines image-only, text-only, and paired data.

document.title: CoCa: Contrastive Captioners are Image-Text Foundation Models
document.abstract: CoCa combines image-text contrastive learning and autoregressive captioning in an encoder-decoder model. Earlier decoder layers encode unimodal text, while later layers attend to images. Sharing computation between objectives supports recognition, retrieval, and generative visual-language tasks.

document.title: PaLI: A Jointly-Scaled Multilingual Language-Image Model
document.abstract: PaLI jointly scales visual and encoder-decoder language models for multilingual multimodal tasks. Text generation provides a common interface for visual and textual inputs. Large multilingual pretraining mixtures and a larger vision backbone are studied for captioning, questions, and related tasks.

document.title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
document.abstract: PaLM-E incorporates visual observations and continuous sensor states into an embodied language model. Multimodal input sequences support robotic manipulation planning alongside visual questions and captions. Joint training examines transfer between embodied tasks and broader language-vision data.

document.title: Image as a Foreign Language: BEiT Pretraining for All Vision and Vision-Language Tasks
document.abstract: BEiT-3 treats images and text as inputs to unified masked modeling. A Multiway Transformer provides both modality-specific processing and multimodal fusion. The pretrained representation transfers to visual recognition, detection, segmentation, captioning, retrieval, and visual reasoning.

document.title: Language Is Not All You Need: Aligning Perception with Language Models
document.abstract: Kosmos-1 is trained on text, image-caption pairs, and interleaved multimodal web documents. The language-modeling framework combines perception with in-context learning and instruction following. Evaluations cover language tasks, visual dialogue, captions, questions, and visual recognition.

document.title: Kosmos-2: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Models to the World
document.abstract: Kosmos-2 extends multimodal language modeling with grounding of textual spans to image locations. Location tokens represent object boxes and grounded image-text pairs support training. Tasks include referring expressions, phrase grounding, and perception-language understanding and generation.

document.title: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All
document.abstract: ImageBind learns a shared representation spanning images, text, audio, depth, thermal signals, and inertial measurements. Training uses pairings with images rather than every possible modality pair. The representation enables cross-modal retrieval, composition, and transfer to additional modalities.

document.title: Otter: A Multi-Modal Model with In-Context Instruction Tuning
document.abstract: Otter adapts OpenFlamingo with multimodal in-context instruction data. The MIMIC-IT dataset combines contextual examples and instructions, supporting both instruction following and contextual learning. The work also makes the underlying training implementation more accessible.

document.title: Improved Baselines with Visual Instruction Tuning
document.abstract: LLaVA-1.5 strengthens visual instruction tuning with a higher-resolution CLIP encoder, an MLP visual-language connector, and academic question-answering data. Simple formatting prompts and publicly available data provide a stronger baseline across multiple multimodal benchmarks.

document.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
document.abstract: SigLIP replaces globally normalized softmax contrastive training with a pairwise sigmoid objective for image-text learning. This separates loss computation from a full batch similarity normalization. Experiments explore batch size and negative-pair choices for efficient language-image pretraining.

document.title: GIT: A Generative Image-to-text Transformer for Vision and Language
document.abstract: GIT uses an image encoder and a text decoder trained with a language-modeling objective. The simplified architecture avoids external detectors, taggers, and OCR modules. Scaling experiments cover image and video captioning, visual questions, and generation-based recognition.

document.title: Unifying Architectures, Tasks, and Modalities Through a Simple Sequence-to-Sequence Learning Framework
document.abstract: OFA casts visual, textual, and cross-modal tasks into an instruction-conditioned encoder-decoder sequence framework. It shares a common architecture across image generation, visual grounding, captions, classification, and language tasks without additional task-specific layers.
